turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Good morning, thanks for calling Acme Life, you're speaking with Mia. Just so you know, this call is recorded for quality and training purposes. How can I help today?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Morning, Mia. I saw your ad in the paper on the weekend, the life cover one. Thought I'd ring and find out a bit more.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Lovely, happy to help with that. Before we get into any of your details or a quote, can I please confirm your full name and date of birth?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Sure. It's Joshua Taylor, Josh is fine. Date of birth is the fourteenth of March, 1959.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Thanks, Josh, that's all confirmed. So, can you tell me a bit about yourself and what's got you thinking about life cover?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Well, I've just retired, taught primary school for thirty-odd years. The house is paid off, my super's ticking along. But I've got four grandkids now and I'd like to leave them a little something. Help with uni or a first car, that sort of thing.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Congratulations on the retirement, that's a big milestone. And that's a really lovely reason. Is there a partner or anyone else who relies on you financially at the moment?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: My wife, Carol, but she's got her own super and she's still working part-time. So it's really more about the grandkids than anyone depending on me.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Got it. And do you have any existing life insurance, maybe through your super?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: I did through my teachers' super fund, but I think it dropped off or reduced when I retired. Honestly I'm not a hundred percent sure.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: That's pretty common. It'd be worth checking with your fund at some point. Do you have a rough figure in mind for what you'd like to leave the grandkids?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: I was thinking maybe twenty-five thousand each? So a hundred thousand all up. Is that silly?

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Not silly at all. Let me explain how the cover works first. With Acme Life Cover you can choose anywhere from fifty thousand up to a million dollars. There's no medical exam, it's just a few health questions, and acceptance depends on your answers.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: No medical? That's good, I'm not keen on being poked and prodded.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Most people feel the same. There are a couple of important things to know, though. In the first twelve months, only accidental death is covered. So if you passed away from an illness in that first year, it wouldn't pay out. After twelve months, you're covered more broadly.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Right. So the first year is basically accidents only.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: That's right. The other thing is the premiums are stepped, which means they go up each year as you get older. So what you pay at sixty-six will be more next year, and more again the year after.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Hmm. That's the bit that worries me a bit. I'm on a fixed income now.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: That's a fair concern. Based on what you've told me, I'd recommend going with the hundred thousand. It lines up with your twenty-five thousand per grandchild, and it keeps the premium more manageable than going higher. I wouldn't go for more than that, given Carol's got her own super and nobody's relying on your income.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Okay. And what would that actually cost me?

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: I'd need to run through the health questions to give you an exact figure. Would you like to do that now? It only takes a few minutes.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Go on then, let's see.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Great. In the last five years, have you been diagnosed with or treated for heart disease, stroke, or cancer?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: No, none of those. I'm on tablets for blood pressure, that's about it.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Thanks. Is your blood pressure well controlled on the medication?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Yep, GP's happy with it. Checked it last month.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Good. And have you smoked any tobacco in the last twelve months?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Gave up in my thirties.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Perfect. Based on those answers, for a hundred thousand dollars of cover your starting premium would be around a hundred and twelve dollars a month. Just keep in mind that's this year's price, and it'll increase each year with age.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: A hundred and twelve a month. So that's over thirteen hundred a year, and going up from there. Gee. I hadn't really thought about how that adds up over time.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: It's definitely worth thinking about. Some people find that if they put the same money into savings for the grandkids, that suits them better. Others prefer knowing the lump sum is there no matter what. There's no right or wrong answer.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Yeah. I think I'd like to talk it over with Carol before I sign up to anything. And maybe check what's still in my super, like you said.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: That sounds really sensible. There's no rush at all. And just so you know for later, if you did take it out, there's a thirty-day cooling-off period where you can cancel and get a full refund.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: That's good to know. Can you send me something in writing so I can show her?

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Of course. I'll email you the product information along with today's quote. What's the best email address for you?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: It's josh.taylor59 at bigpond dot com.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Thanks, Josh, that's josh.taylor59 at bigpond dot com. You'll have that within the hour. Whenever you and Carol have had a chance to look through it, just give us a call back on the number in the email.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Will do. Thanks for not giving me the hard sell, Mia.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: My pleasure. Enjoy the retirement, and say hi to the grandkids. Have a lovely day.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: You too. Bye now.
